review-rework-settings-panel.title: Review-return loop (REVIEW-REWORK)
review-rework-settings-panel.description: A review verdict that returns a pull request (RETURN) opens a rework task for the PR's author and blocks the review on it; a new head in the PR releases the review back to its reviewer, and a merged or closed PR settles the review. The switch and the fallback executor apply without a restart — the sweep re-reads them on every pass.
review-rework-settings-panel.enabledHint: Off leaves the board as it was: a RETURN verdict creates no task and the review keeps waking on an unchanged PR.
review-rework-settings-panel.fallbackPlaceholder: Empty = the role queue claims it
review-rework-settings-panel.fallbackHint: The rework first goes to the PR's author (the review's return assignee), then to the assignee of the task the PR delivers. This is the last rung; empty means nobody — an unassigned todo task, which the role queue of SWARM-CLAIM claims.
review-rework-settings-panel.fallbackError: Enter an agent UUID, or leave it empty for the role queue

run-stall-settings-panel.title: Run stall detection
run-stall-settings-panel.description: The sweep that interrupts a running run whose own recorded progress stopped advancing: the task goes back to todo and the assignee is woken. A run working for hours with fresh progress is never touched — this is not a duration limit. Saving takes effect immediately, without a restart. Whether the sweep runs and its silence threshold are set in the <link>Team liveness settings</link> (one source of truth for all three liveness passes); they are shown here read-only.
run-stall-settings-panel.readOnlyHint: Read-only here: change them in the Team liveness settings (runStallEnabled, runStallThresholdSec).

checkIntervalSec.label: Sweep interval, seconds
checkIntervalSec.hint: Minimum spacing between two scan passes; the scheduler queue itself ticks more often. From 15; default 60.

pageSize.label: Page size
pageSize.hint: How many running runs one scan pass inspects at most, stalest progress first. From 1 to 200; default 50.

runtime-limits-settings-panel.title: Run limits
runtime-limits-settings-panel.description: How many agent runs this server starts at once, how fast, and how much memory it and the host keep free. A run over a ceiling waits in the queue and starts when a slot frees. Saving takes effect immediately: queued runs start within a minute and no running run is interrupted. Leave a field empty to switch that limit off.

maxConcurrentRuns.label: Concurrent runs
maxConcurrentRuns.hint: Runs this server starts at once. Runs over the ceiling stay queued and start when a slot frees.

maxStartsPerMinute.label: Starts per minute (start ramp)
maxStartsPerMinute.hint: How many runs may start in a sliding minute, so a restart, a bulk resolve or a mass wake does not start everything in one burst. Default 5.

minFreeMemoryMb.label: Free memory to keep, MB
minFreeMemoryMb.hint: A run starts only if the server container keeps this much memory free after it. This is the hard floor: below it everything waits, including the answer to a message the owner wrote in a chat. That answer is held by this floor alone — measured on the container and on the host's available memory — and not by the host floor below. Default 1500.

runMemoryEstimateMb.label: Memory per run, MB
runMemoryEstimateMb.hint: What one run is budgeted when free memory is counted.

minFreeHostMemoryMb.label: Free host memory to keep, MB
minFreeHostMemoryMb.hint: A new run starts only while the host (where the bot containers run) has at least this much available memory; otherwise it waits in the queue. The automatic runs wait here — a turn started by a message the owner wrote in a chat does not: it is admitted by the floor above (applied to the container and to the host's available memory) and goes to the front of the queue. Default 15360 (15 GB).

maxHostLoadPercentPerCore.label: Max host load per core, % of a core
maxHostLoadPercentPerCore.hint: A new run starts only while the host's 1-minute load average is this many percent of one CPU core ABOVE the load the host carries on its own (100 = one core fully busy). The host's own background — the services that keep it busy without any run — does not close the ceiling: only the load the runs add counts. A turn started by a message the owner wrote in a chat does not wait for this ceiling either. Default 90. Empty switches the ceiling off.

fairShare.label: Single-agent start share, % per 10 min
fairShare.hint: The most starts one agent may take in a 10-minute window, in percent. Past its share its new runs wait until the other agents have had their turn, so a hot agent cannot occupy the queue. Default 15. Empty switches the limit off (100 = no limit).

team-liveness-health-card.title: Team liveness

autoResumes.label: Auto-resumes
autoResumes.hint: Agents the board brought back out of error by itself

autoResumeExhaustions.label: Resumes given up
autoResumeExhaustions.hint: Attempts ran out — these need a human look

wakes.label: Wakes
wakes.hint: Wakes the board created for this company

stalledRuns.label: Stalled runs
stalledRuns.hint: Runs that stopped making progress and were interrupted

emptyRuns.label: Empty runs
emptyRuns.hint: Runs that finished only with a comment and without a commit, PR, or status change. API includes per-agent counts.

team-liveness-health-card.footnote: What the board did on its own for this company in the window. A run of "Resumes given up" or "Stalled runs" means an agent needs a human look; the switches behind all four sit in the Team liveness panel.

team-liveness-settings-panel.title: Team liveness
team-liveness-settings-panel.description: What the board does on its own when a run fails, when a run stops making progress, and when an agent sits idle with ready work. The three sweeps read these values on their next pass: saving takes effect without a restart and without dropping a run in flight. A field you do not change keeps coming from the server environment. An agent card can switch a behaviour off for that one agent.

autoResumeEnabled.label: Auto-resume an agent left in error
autoResumeEnabled.hint: The board resumes an agent whose run failed, with backoff, instead of leaving it in error until an operator acts.

runStallEnabled.label: Interrupt a run that stops making progress
runStallEnabled.hint: A run that records no progress for the stall threshold is interrupted, its task goes back to the queue and its assignee is woken.

idlePickupEnabled.label: Wake an idle agent that has ready work
idlePickupEnabled.hint: The board wakes an agent that is idle while a ready task is assigned to it, so the team does not wait for a reassignment by hand.

runStallThresholdSec.label: Stall threshold, seconds
runStallThresholdSec.hint: How long a running run may record no progress before it counts as stalled. Default 1200 (20 minutes).

idlePickupIntervalSec.label: Wake pass interval, seconds
idlePickupIntervalSec.hint: How often the board looks for an idle agent with ready work. Default 30.

idlePickupWakeBudgetPerMin.label: Wakes per minute, whole company
idlePickupWakeBudgetPerMin.hint: The company-wide ceiling on automatic wakes: every wake is a full agent run. Default 5.

idlePickupWakeBatch.label: Wakes per pass
idlePickupWakeBatch.hint: How many of that minute's wakes one pass may spend at once; the rest wait for the next pass. Never above the minute ceiling. Default 5.

tool-policy-cache-settings-panel.title: Tool gateway policy cache
tool-policy-cache-settings-panel.description: The tool gateway keeps one snapshot of a company's tool policies, profiles, bindings and profile entries in memory instead of reading four tables on every call. A change made through the board shows up on the very next decision; this window only bounds changes written to the database by other means. Saving applies to the next gateway call without a restart. 0 switches the cache off.
